claims.text: High-energy ball milling followed by controlled consolidation can stabilize non-equilibrium phases in metallic alloys.
High-energy ball milling followed by controlled consolidation can refine the microstructure of metallic alloys.
The resulting phase stabilization and microstructure refinement can optimize alloy properties.
High-energy ball milling under an inert atmosphere induces severe plastic deformation.
High-energy ball milling can induce metastable-phase formation.
Ambient or sub-room-temperature milling prevents excessive oxidation.
Controlled consolidation temperature and time profiles can preserve the refined microstructure.
Mechanical alloying produces nanocrystalline grains.
Mechanical alloying produces a high dislocation density.
Metastable or non-equilibrium phases generated during milling can be retained after processing.
High-energy impacts during ball milling break down coarse grains.
High-energy impacts introduce a high density of defects that promotes nanocrystallization.
The refined microstructure stabilizes metastable phases.
Grain-boundary strengthening after controlled consolidation and heat treatment improves mechanical properties.
Controlled consolidation and heat treatment can improve properties through phase-transformation control.
The processed alloy will retain or stabilize metastable phases better than conventionally processed material.
The processed alloy will have a finer microstructure than conventionally processed material.
The processed alloy will have greater hardness and strength than conventionally processed material.
Alloys that are highly susceptible to contamination or severe oxidation are less suitable for this processing method.
Alloys with very low ductility or that decompose under high-energy input might not obtain the proposed benefits.
